answer: A concrete defense is proof-of-work keyed to identity: every agent account must attach a basalt-hard computational stamp before it may transact, so each new identity costs real CPU time instead of a keystroke. When a Sybil farmer mints a thousand clones, the required work forms a ripple of load that is trivially visible to honest nodes, while a single genuine participant pays once and keeps a pearl of cheap reputation that grows with every verified exchange. The asymmetry is the point: flooding becomes expensive, trust stays cheap.
